title: Watch Jobs
markdown:
The **watch** module (`openexecutive.watch`) runs **watch jobs**: unattended ERPNext runs, defined in code, that read a fixed set of ERPNext data, apply rules in code and leave notices and draft cards. A job never runs the Executive's tool loop, never lets a model choose a read, and never writes a figure or a card's field a model made up: a model writes only short reason lines. Two jobs are listed: **collections** (who to chase today, and the payment reminders due) and **payment checks** (a likely duplicate supplier invoice held before it's paid, and a changed bank account flagged for a phone call).

### The registry (`watch.registry`), code only

- A job is a `WatchJob(id, title, reads, build, schedule, card_cap_day, default_settings, reason_schema=None, check_fields=None, setting_bounds={}, card_noun="drafts", slots=(), weekdays=all)`. Its id is oe_connector's `[a-z0-9-]{1,40}`, the key of the job's listing in `oe_connector_watch_jobs` and of its ERP user `oe-watch-<id>@<site>`.
- `reads` is a tuple of `WatchRead(tool, shape, arguments, label)`: an oe_connector tool, the shape of its arguments as oe_connector lists it (a literal matches only the same JSON type and value, so `true` is never `1` and `1.0` never `1`; a slot `$company`, `$date` (an ISO date within 400 days), `$party`, `$parties` / `$customers` (up to 50 names), `$int` (1–500) takes any value of its type; the top-level `fields` list is the most a call may ask for; any other list matches a list of the same length element by element, such as `["<=", "$date"]` or `["in", "$parties"]`, never "any list"; an object has exactly its keys), the code that builds the run's arguments, and how a notice names it.
- **Dependent reads.** `arguments(settings, today, prior)` gets the earlier reads' results (their `acting` removed). A derived list that comes out empty returns `None`: the read is **skipped**, never sent with an empty list, `build` gets `{}` for it, and the run records `{"read", "skipped": true}`. A list cut to its first 50 by the job's own order comes back as `Derived(arguments, truncated=True)`, recorded `truncated`. A derived argument is shape-checked like any other before the call, and oe_connector checks it again as the job's user.
- **Sound shapes only** (oe_connector's own rules, ladislav-urban/oe_connector#536): a `$` string that isn't a slot, a list or object inside a list, a slot in a list anywhere but `[operator, slot]` (`= != < <= > >=` before a single-value slot, `in` / `not in` before `$parties` or `$customers` only), or a list slot as a filter's value on its own makes a read unsound, and `WatchJob` refuses the job when it is defined. Both checkers are tested against oe_connector's own `watch_shape_vectors.json` (its soundness cases, its match cases and their slot oracle).
- **Slots.** A job runs once a day at `schedule`, or at each of its `slots` (times, in order, the first its schedule) on its `weekdays`.
- Any job may list `run_report` and `list_records`. A tool the gateway withholds from every turn (`connected_systems.ERPNEXT_WITHHELD_TOOLS`) may be listed only by the job `JOB_WITHHELD_EXCEPTIONS` gives it to: `customer_payment_record` by collections alone, `supplier_bank_changed` by payment checks alone (chat never reads it, whoever asks). `WatchJob.__post_init__` refuses any other listing, so the registry mirrors the gateway's one exception.
- `build(results, settings, today)` is pure code returning notices (`CardSpec(key, summary, values, facts, items, notes, count)`: `items` are its rows, each a finding of its own for the reason step; `notes` are lines in code's own words) and draft cards (`DraftSpec(key, operation, doctype, fields, expect, title, reason_key, group, name, notice)`: `name` is the document a change or a block is on, `notice` the finding told as a notice when no card can be left for it). `check_fields(operation, doctype, fields, name)` is the job's own builder of a card's fields; it runs before each check and again at approval, so a tampered card is refused.
- Settings are exactly the job's `default_settings` keys and types; a whole number is 1–500 unless `setting_bounds` gives it others (collections' `min_amount` 0 up to a billion).
- `JOBS` is read-only and holds only what the module lists (`_LISTED`: collections and payment checks). Nothing adds a job from settings, chat or an API; the test job `watch.jobs._example` is put in by the tests. `tests/unit/watch_job_vectors.json` pins the id pattern, slot names, shapes, both jobs' reads and one signed `watch` assertion against oe_connector.

### Settings (`watch.settings`, table `watch_jobs`)

One row per job: `enabled` (off by default), `settings` (JSON, checked as above), `configured_by_person_id` and `configured_at`, and an optional `reviewer_person_id`: the person the job's notices and draft cards go to, when the run's routing allows (below). Only the principal changes a row, through `PUT /watch/jobs/{id}` (a signed principal or local login's operator; see API Reference), which records who did it and writes a private `watch_job_configured` audit row. The reviewer must be an active team member who is neither the principal (who configures every job, and never approves its cards) nor a demo person: 400 otherwise. `GET /watch/jobs` carries `reviewer_note`, what Settings says beside the reviewer: they see the job's notices, with the figures ERPNext read as the job's own user, and approve its cards. No chat action calls either route. `ERPNEXT_WATCH_JOBS_ENABLED` (off) is the operator's master switch: off, no job runs whatever its row says.

### The read marker and the gateway

Each read runs inside `erpnext_caller.watch_run(job, tool, arguments)`, a marker code sets and no tool can. It is bound to a job that is registered and on, one of the tools it lists, and the digest of the call's exact arguments, which must fit the read's shape. It is refused (`WatchRefused`, a reason code) while a turn's session is bound, while any other marker is set (the brief's, the oversight export's, the answer check's, a supplier's, a draft's or a job's check, or another watch read's), and without `ERPNEXT_CALLER_PRIVATE_KEY` (`watch-needs-keys`). It saves the marker it found and puts it back on exit.

Inside it `caller_for` answers `ErpnextCaller("watch", job=<id>)` before any session logic, and only alone. `mint` signs `kind: "watch"` with `sub` the job's id, never a `purpose`, and refuses any draft tool. The gateway refuses every other call inside the marker (`outside-watch-read`), compares the arguments' digest after its own argument coercion, and re-checks at call time that no turn and no other marker is bound. A withheld tool is refused on every path but one (`mcp_gateway._job_reads_withheld`): inside `watch_run`, with exactly that tool bound, for the job `JOB_WITHHELD_EXCEPTIONS` gives it to, with no turn and no other marker. Chat, ERPNext's panel, the brief, a supplier's agent, every draft marker and any other job's read are still refused, and tool search never shows it.

oe_connector checks the job is listed and the call fits one of its listed reads, as the job's own narrow ERP user when the job is set `as_job_user`, else the OE Reader service view, and reports which in the result's top-level `acting` (`{kind, job, as_job_user, user}`). The runner reads only that top-level key: per read, whether it ran as exactly `oe-watch-<job>@<site>`, the same user on every read; `acting.job` naming another job ends the run.

### The job's check marker (`draft_check_for_job`)

A job's draft card is checked by ERPNext **as the job's reviewer**, so its summary and fingerprint are what the reviewer can see, and approval later runs as the same person. `erpnext_caller.draft_check_for_job(job, arguments, email, person_id=, day=)` marks the one `erpnext__draft_check` call (`DraftCall.unattended`, with the job and the reviewer's person id), signed `kind: "user"`, `purpose: "draft"` as the reviewer. It is refused (`JobCheckRefused`, a code) under a turn's session or any other marker (a watch read's included: it never nests, and no draft marker can be set inside it), without the caller key, for a job that isn't registered and on, unless the arguments are `{operation, doctype, [name,] fields}` with the fields exactly as the job's `check_fields` builds them (`draft_check` takes nothing else, so never `asked_by` or `configured_by`), unless the person is the job's current reviewer under that email (active, on the team, not a demo person, not the principal), and past the day's cap (two runs' worth of `card_cap_day` checks plus 2 retries, counted in `watch_days.checks`, so a restart never resets it and a refused check still counts). The gateway refuses any other tool under it (`outside-job-check`), refuses it under a session or a watch read, and reads the reviewer again from People and the job's row when it signs.

### The runner (`watch.runner`)

- **Once a day, or at each slot.** A scheduler tick hook (`maybe_run`) starts each job that is on, on its weekdays, once one of its slots is due in the company's time zone (collections at 07:00, before the brief; payment checks hourly 08:00–18:00, Monday to Friday), when it wins that slot's claim: a `watch_runs` row keyed `(job, day, slot)` (`slot` "HH:MM", "" for a daily job; `status`, `started_at`, `attempts`, `cards`, `error`, `reads`, `detail`) taken under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. Only the latest due slot is claimed: earlier ones with no row are marked `skipped` in the same transaction, so a worker down for three hours runs once, not three times. A run left `running` for 30 minutes is retried once while its slot is still the latest due, then failed; one a later slot has overtaken is failed (`run_overtaken`), never retried, and a later slot waits while an earlier run is still fresh. A day whose hour daylight saving skipped still runs. A `watch_runs` table from before slots is migrated once, its rows kept with slot "". `watch_days (job, day, cards, failure_noticed, checks)` counts the day's draft cards, and the checks made as the reviewer, each in one transaction across slots, workers and restarts, and lets a job leave one failure notice a calendar day. Each run is one task of its own, with no session and no audit scope, under the turn id `watch:<id>:<day>` and the job's cost budget once cost caps are in.
- **Reads.** Each read's arguments are built by the job's code (skipped or truncated as above) and checked against its shape before the call. A refused or failed read ends the run: the principal gets one notice a day naming the read and why, in our words, and nothing partial is raised. A refusal naming `oe_connector_bank_facts` (ladislav-urban/oe_connector#534) says "Supplier bank checks are off in ERPNext's settings." The run's row, the log and the audit hold a reason code only, never ERPNext's text.
- **Rules.** `job.build` turns the results into notices and draft cards. At most 200 findings a run.
- **Routing** (`watch.cards.route`), from the database and oe_connector's own word, never a model or a read's result. The run goes to the job's reviewer only when every read made (at least one; a skipped read counts neither way) ran as the job's own user, the reviewer's People row is active, on the team, not a demo person, not the principal, not whoever configured the job, and has an email, and teammates' drafts (`ERPNEXT_DRAFTS_TEAMMATES`) and signed sign-ins are on. Otherwise the principal gets the notices only, and the run records why (`detail.routed_principal`: `no_reads`, `not_job_user`, `no_reviewer`, `reviewer_unavailable`, `reviewer_is_configurer`, `teammates_off`, `signing_off`).
- **Reasons** (a job with a `reason_schema`): one tool-less call to the fast utility model with its own constant system prompt (`REASON_SYSTEM`), shown the notices' rows (each finding's bounded facts, at most 20) wrapped as untrusted and keyed by short ids. Only a JSON object of reasons for the ids it was shown is kept, each cleaned and at most 200 characters. A reason is labelled as a model's words, never as a figure, and never reaches a key, a title, a card's fields or routing.
- **Cards** (`watch.cards.leave_drafts`), only once routing named the reviewer: no check is ever made for a run that went to the principal. A kind of card that is off on this server (a DocType not listed for drafts or changes, a block while any of its three switches is off) isn't proposed. For each `DraftSpec` in the job's order: none while the same finding's card waits or once one was left that day; at most `card_cap_day` a day, across the day's slots (taken before the check, given back when no card is left); at most 10 of the job's cards waiting; and never the reviewer past `OPEN_CARDS_MAX` less 5, so their own asks still fit. ERPNext checks each card as the reviewer under the check marker; the check must read back the card the job built (a new draft: the operation, the DocType and what the job expects, as collections' invoice, customer and company; a change: the same document and change, and a draft that is the reviewer's own or assigned to them; a block: that invoice, the one it repeats, the card's release date, its supplier and company) and give a fingerprint, or no card is left. A finding with no card is told as its notice, when the job gave one. Each check writes a private `watch_job_check` audit row (job, day, operation, person id, a result code, never ERPNext's text). A refused check leaves no card, and the notice says how many in code's words ("… couldn't be prepared as <reviewer>: their ERPNext access doesn't allow it"). When every check of a run was refused for the reviewer's permissions, the run's notice goes to the principal.
- **Notices.** Private alerts (source `watch`, `needs: fyi`) stored directly, never through triage: routed as above. The headline is code only (the job's title and counts); every ERPNext string in the body is stripped and capped, the body is wrapped `wrap_untrusted(source="erpnext", author="watch:<id>")`, each row is shown with its reason ("Why now", a model's words), and code's own lines follow the block: the job's notes, how many cards wait for whom, and why none were prepared ("Name a reviewer in Settings → Watch jobs to get the reminder drafts."). A finding whose notice is still open isn't raised again, nor one already raised that day.
- **Audit.** One private `watch_run` row per run: status, reason code and counts (notices, cards left, repeats, capped, checks, refused), who it went to; never ERPNext's figures or text.

### Job draft cards and separation of duties (`integrations.erpnext_drafts`)

- **Left in code**, never through `propose_erpnext_draft` or triage: `leave_job_card` goes through the same `propose` as every card (the digest dedupe, a new fingerprint replacing the waiting card, never a card changed in place), scoped to the job so a person's own chat card is never one of them, with `source: "watch"`, `job`, `run_day`, `asked_by` (the reviewer's email the check ran as), `asked_by_person_id`, `approver_person_id` (the reviewer), `configured_by_person_id` (who configured the job when the run left it), the finding's `dedup_key` and the reason line. Its headline is code's; the card shows the job's title ("Dunning draft from the Collections job") and the reason as "Why now: …".
- **Approval** (`_job_approval`, before anything is claimed), besides every card's own checks: **separation of duties first, whatever `ERPNEXT_DRAFT_SOD` says**: the approver is neither the card's configurer nor the job's current one, and the configurer's People row still exists, is active and has an email; otherwise "You set up this job, so someone else approves its cards. Nothing was made." and the card closes as `sod_refused`, audited (`erpnext_draft_sod_refused`). Then the job is registered and on (master switch and row), the approver is not the principal or a demo person, is the card's stored approver and the job's current reviewer, the fields are exactly what the job's `check_fields` builds (a Dunning with its letter date), and the fingerprint is there.
- **The wire values** come from the stored keys, never a model: the write tool gets `asked_by: "job:<id>"` and `configured_by`, the configurer's **current** People email, resolved at approval, with `expected_fingerprint`. `draft_check` never gets either. oe_connector applies its own separation of duties when the site's `oe_connector_draft_sod` is `agent`; its refusal closes the card the same way.

### Collections (`watch.jobs.collections`)

- **Reads**, as listed in oe_connector: Accounts Receivable by due date for the company on the day (up to 500 rows); the Dunnings sent (submitted, with customer, date, type and the invoices each covered) and those still in draft (up to 500 each); and `customer_payment_record` for the overdue customers, the 50 largest by amount × days, derived from the first read (skipped when nobody is overdue).
- **Rules** (code, tested on fixed data): who to chase, in order: the largest and longest debts first (at least the median overdue amount, 60 days or more), then a usually prompt customer late for the first time (3 or more settled invoices in 12 months, none late), then the rest; each by amount × days, then amount, then name. An invoice is due for a reminder when it is `first_after_days` (7) overdue with none sent, or its last reminder is more than `repeat_after_days` (14) old; the type is `type_first` for the first and `type_repeat` after (empty: the company's default). Never a reminder for a customer with a Dunning in draft, below `min_amount`, listed in `phone_only`, or whose payment record couldn't be read (`not_shown`, or beyond the 50 asked about; such a customer is ranked without the "usually prompt" step, and the notice says so). A truncated Dunning list leaves no cards that day.
- **Outputs:** one "Who to chase today" notice (up to 10 customers: amount, days, invoices, how they pay, reminders sent and due, the rank's rule, and a reason line each), and a Dunning card per (customer, invoice) due, in ranking order, at most 5 a day, deduped per invoice and Dunning Type, its fields `{sales_invoice, dunning_type, posting_date}` with the letter date from ERPNext's check. The card reuses the Dunning card's view and executor; only `asked_by` and `configured_by` come from the job.

### Payment checks (`watch.jobs.payment_checks`)

- **When:** every hour from 08:00 to 18:00, Monday to Friday, company time; at most 10 cards a day across the hours. Settings: `company`, `due_within_days` (14, 1–400), `block_submitted` (off).
- **Reads**, as listed in oe_connector: the company's unpaid Purchase Invoices due within `due_within_days`, drafts and submitted (`list_records`, `docstatus ["<", 2]`, `outstanding_amount [">", 0]`, `due_date ["<=", $date]`); the same suppliers' submitted invoices of the last 120 days (`supplier ["in", $parties]`, the 50 soonest due); and `supplier_bank_changed` for them. Both derived reads are skipped when nothing is due.
- **Duplicates** (code, the same rules oe_connector's block applies): the same supplier and currency, both with a supplier invoice date, and the same bill number once normalized (case, spaces, dashes, leading zeros), a real one, with the same amount or dates within 60 days (**high**); or the same amount and bill date (**medium**); or the same amount within 3 days (**low**, a notice only, never proposed). The copy is a draft against a submitted invoice, or the later posted of two submitted ones, unpaid and not already on hold.
- **A duplicate draft:** a hold card (`draft_update`: `on_hold` 1 and a `hold_comment` from code's template, "Possible duplicate of <other>: same bill number" or "… same amount and date", cleaned, at most 280 characters), only when ERPNext's check as the reviewer says the draft is theirs or assigned to them; otherwise a notice.
- **A duplicate submitted invoice:** a notice saying to use Block Invoice in ERPNext, or, with the job's `block_submitted`, `ERPNEXT_BLOCK_INVOICE` and the pinned `draft_block_invoice` all on, a block card (`integrations.erpnext_block`): `draft_check` with operation `block` and `{duplicate_of, release_date}` (the run's day plus 14), showing ERPNext's figures for both invoices, the payments under way and "held until someone unblocks it, at the latest <release date>".
- **A changed bank account** (changed after the last payment, or never paid with details from the last 30 days): a notice with code's own line, "Confirm the change with the supplier by phone, on a number you already have, before paying."
- **Approving a block** re-checks all three switches first (409 `block_off`, nothing claimed), separation of duties, and `{duplicate_of, release_date}` (after today, at most 90 days ahead). It sends `{name, duplicate_of, release_date, idempotency_key, asked_by: "job:payment-checks", configured_by, expected_fingerprint}`, only for the payment-checks job's card. A changed invoice, separation of duties, a blocking limit, an invoice a person unblocked before, or a block not from the job's card closes the card. `erpnext_changes.enabled("block")` lists nothing, so chat and ERPNext's panel can never propose one.
